name: Week 23 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Cable Crunch + Reverse Fly)
description:
Pull day, spotlights cycle to the cable crunch and the reverse fly — the two that have quietly been running without a real cue pass.

Equipment is corrected from last week's flags: face pull is on the **adjustable pulley + rope** (where it's always been), the high cable curl has its **load numbers back**, and the lat pulldown lists the **dual-pulley number (70/side)** you settled on.

The slow eccentric stays the organizing idea. Pull-ups and DB row hold their tempo work; the incline curl keeps left-first while the left side is still telling its story.

dayOverview.theme: Spotlights rotate to the cable crunch and the reverse fly. Equipment corrected: face pull on the adjustable pulley + rope, high cable curl load restored, lat pulldown dual-pulley number listed. Slow eccentric stays across the day; pull-ups and DB row hold their tempo; incline curl keeps left-first.

spotlights.why: It's held 67.5 'felt strong today' and mostly gets logged as an afterthought, which is a shame because the cable crunch is one of the few direct-loaded ab movements you run and it rewards a real cue. The spotlight is the distinction that makes it work: the spine flexes, the hips don't. Most cable crunches quietly turn into a hip-hinge with the arms pulling the weight; the fix is to crunch the ribcage toward the pelvis and leave the hips out of it, which is where the abs actually earn the 67.5.

This one's been drifting on equipment — 20s, then 25s when the 20s were taken — and running on 'did ok,' which means it's overdue for a pass on what actually matters: the rear delt, not the weight. It's a small muscle in a position that's easy to cheat with momentum or by turning it into a row. The spotlight is soft fixed elbows, lead with the elbows, and a slow squeeze — pick a weight you can own that way and note which, so it stops floating.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Pull spotlights rotate: W21 chest-supported row + incline curl · W22 pull-up + DB row tempo · W23 cable crunch + reverse fly (current) · W24 back to lat pulldown + face pull.
watchpoints: **🔆 Cable crunch: spine flexes, hips DON'T** 🔥. Crunch the ribs toward the pelvis; don't hip-hinge or arm-pull. Rope pulley 67.5-77.5 OR cable column ~270 — pick by availability, log which. The cue is the work.
**🔆 Reverse fly: soft fixed elbows, lead with the elbows, slow squeeze** 🔥. Pick a weight you can own that way (20 or 25) and NOTE which. Rear delt, not a row.
**Face pull is on the ADJUSTABLE PULLEY + ROPE at 50** 🔥 — corrected from the 'cable column' label. Elbows high, knuckles up. 'Best non-event one you've done' last week.
**High cable curl** — cable column 170-180 OR single pulley 62.5 (pick by availability, log which). Left arm first.
**Lat pulldown: dual pulley 70/side (140) is the settled number** 🛑; 80/side (160) was over the top last week. Regular machine 150 if you're on it.
**Pull-ups hold the slow eccentric** 🛑 — 8/8/8/6 last week, set 4 ending clean not falling apart. 'No pain just weak' is the ideal — grip/back is the ceiling, shoulder's fine.
**DB row 70/80/90 pyramid** 🛑 — left grip slipped at 8 on the 90 last week; that's the honest number, no straps.
**Incline curl keeps left-first, no new cue** 🛑 — left's been the harder arm two weeks running but completing the reps. Still just watching.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure last set OK — cable crunch, reverse fly, chest-supported row, face pull, high cable curl. 🛑 keep it shy — pull-up, DB row, lat pulldown, incline curl.
**Behind-back shrug goes FIRST. Cool-down is 5 min, not optional.**

exercises.notes: **The pull-day shoulder anchor.** Slow, blades together, no momentum.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked — grip primer.
Passive hang. Decompress and wake the grip.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets, first in the session.
- Held behind the body, palms back
- **Blades DOWN and BACK**, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down
- Decompresses the right shoulder before anything loads it

sets.name: Pull-Ups — Straight Bar (4 Sets, Slow Eccentric) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** bodyweight, straight bar, 4 sets.
- **3s eccentric** on every rep of sets 1-3
- **Pack DOWN before you pull** — blades into the back pockets, elbows drive to the ribs
- **Chest to the bar**, full hang at the bottom
- **No straps** — grip is part of the lift
- Last week was 8/8/8/6 ending clean, 'no pain just weak' — the shoulder's a non-issue, grip/back is the honest ceiling. Hold the tempo; let set 4 be what it is

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row 🛑 + Chest-Supported Row 🔥 + Incline Curl 🛑 + Reverse Fly (Spotlight) 🔥 (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70 / 80 / 90 ascending pyramid — one set per round.
- **Pack DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves, elbow past the ribs
- **The 90 set can go slow** if the grip holds — left slipped at 8 last week, right stopped at 8 to match
- **No straps.** The left-grip-limited 8 at 90 IS the honest number

**LOAD:** 45. 3 sets. 🔥
- **All sets slow eccentric**, and add the pause you flagged ('could do slower with pause')
- Chest stays on the pad, no heaving
- Squeeze the blades, slow return to a full stretch

**LOAD:** 25lb DBs, incline bench. **Start LEFT.**
- **Elbow stays behind the torso** — that's the incline's job
- **Full stretch at the bottom**, no swinging
- Left's been harder two weeks running but completing the reps — keep left-first, no other change

**LOAD:** 20lb (or 25 if the 20s are taken — NOTE which). 3 sets. 🔥

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — rear delt, not a row:**
- **Chest supported, soft FIXED elbows** — the angle doesn't change through the rep
- **Lead with the elbows**, slow squeeze of the rear delts at the top
- **Slow eccentric** while you have it; normal tempo once tired is fine
- Pick the weight you can own with fixed elbows and **write down which**

**Reflection:** is the rear delt doing it, or are you rowing/momentum-ing the weight up? Small muscle, clean line — that's the lift.

sets.notes: 3 rounds — all four lifts around the adjustable benches.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- **Dual pulley: 70/side (≈140 total)** — the settled number (80/side was over the top last week: 10/6)
- Regular lat pulldown machine: **150**
- Cable column: 52.5-57.5

- **Pack DOWN first** — blades into the back pockets before the bar moves
- **Bar to the upper chest**, elbows driving down and back, no leaning back
- Slow return, full stretch at the top

Pick whichever's free; **note the station + number.** 'Feels good on shoulders' on this lift lately.

sets.name: Face Pull — Adjustable Pulley + Rope (3 Sets at 50) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** adjustable pulley + rope **50** (settled). 3 sets of 20. 🔥
- **Rope to the forehead**, elbows HIGH and wide
- **External rotation at the end** — thumbs back, knuckles up
- **Pack down** — traps quiet
- Slow eccentric — 'best non-event one you've done' last week. Light and high-rep on purpose; shoulder health

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (Spotlight) 🔥

exercises.equipment: cable column OR single pulley — whichever's free
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, pick by availability, LOG which station):**
- Cable column (D-handle): **170-180**
- Single pulley: **62.5**
- **Stand sideways, upper arm PARALLEL to the floor and FIXED** — the elbow doesn't drop
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**, slow eccentric, no bounce. Shoulder-friendly, it's been clean

**LOAD (rope attachment; pick by availability, LOG which):**
- Cable pulley (rope): **67.5-77.5** (77.5 is the strong reference)
- Cable column: **~270** (the pulley's leverage makes these two match)

3 sets. 🔥

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — spine flexes, hips stay put:**
- **Crunch the ribcage toward the pelvis** — the spine flexes, the HIPS DON'T move
- **Don't hip-hinge** and don't pull with the arms — the arms just hold the rope
- Slow return, no yanking
- Read the stack — magnetic micro add-ons can be on without noticing

**Reflection:** are the abs crunching, or are the hips folding and the arms pulling? Ribs-to-pelvis with still hips is the whole lift.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow height.
Passive. Second hang of the day — let the grip release.

tips: **Cable crunch spotlight: spine flexes, hips don't.** Ribs to pelvis, arms just hold. 67.5 stays.
**Reverse fly spotlight: rear delt, not a row.** Soft fixed elbows, slow squeeze; note which weight (20 or 25).
**Face pull is on the adjustable pulley + rope at 50** — equipment corrected.
**High cable curl** — cable column 170-180 OR single pulley 62.5, pick by availability. Left first, log the station.
**Lat pulldown: dual pulley 70/side, or machine 150.** 80/side was over the top last week.
**Pull-ups hold the slow eccentric**; DB row 70/80/90 pyramid, no straps.
🔥 near-failure OK on cable crunch, reverse fly, chest-supported row, face pull, high cable curl. 🛑 keep it shy on pull-up, DB row, lat pulldown, incline curl.
formPhilosophy: The two lifts under the spotlight this week are the two most likely to quietly turn into something they aren't — a cable crunch that's become a hip-hinge, a reverse fly that's become a row. Neither shows up as a problem in the log because both still 'work'; they just stop working the muscle they're for. That's the failure mode a form-first program has to actually look for, because it never announces itself as a missed rep. And the equipment corrections matter for the same reason the loads do: a number is only honest if you know which machine it's on. Fix the label, keep the weight, spotlight the cheat. Building decades, not weeks.
